title: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
summary: Kuka asks who a person is. Kuka sinä olet? — Minä olen Anna.
targetSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
objectives: Ask who one person is with kuka.
Answer with the correct speaker, listener or other-person form.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun.
Kuka asks who a person is. In a neutral question, put kuka first: Kuka sinä olet? (“Who are you?”). Do not add -ko/-kö.
keyPoints: Do not ask a person's identity with mikä in these examples.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Answer from your own point of view: sinä olet (“you are”) in the question becomes minä olen (“I am”) in your reply. Hän on stays hän on when both speakers mean the same other person. Minä and sinä may be omitted with olen and olet; keep hän when referring to another person. In a role game, Kuka minä olen? (“Who am I?”) receives Sinä olet… (“You are…”), because the reply addresses the original speaker.
A natural short reply to “Kuka sinä olet?” is “Anna.” (“Anna.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
When correcting a mistaken identity, first reject the wrong name and then give the actual identity. The complete negative phrase en ole means I am not.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Match the singular reply to its speaker: minä olen, sinä olet, hän on. Check who the reply describes before choosing the person form.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: olen means I am here. Olla has the I-form olen: ole- + -n. The ending identifies the speaker.
on means is here. Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
olet means you are here. Olla has the singular you-form olet: ole- + -t.
keyPoints: Match the singular reply to its speaker: minä olen, sinä olet, hän on. Check who the reply describes before choosing the person form.

examples.finnish: Minä en ole Anna. Minä olen Mikko.
examples.english: I am not Anna. I am Mikko.
steps: Minä: I; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Minä is the singular first-person subject pronoun, used by a speaker about themself.
en: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
Anna: Anna; identity or category given after olla. Anna is a person's name and keeps its basic form as a subject or identity.
olen: I am; verb (the action or state). Olla has the I-form olen: ole- + -n. The ending identifies the speaker.
Mikko: Mikko; identity or category given after olla. Mikko is a person's name and keeps its basic form here.
